title: Experimental Analysis of Receiver Design for Near-Field Coordinated Beamforming.
abstract: Next-generation wireless networks are envisioned to operate in sub-THz bands to enable increased data rates and sensing resolution. In such bands, Coordinated Beamforming (CoBF) will be a critical technique to mitigate performance degradation that can occur when highly directional links are occluded by mobile environmental obstructions. Moreover, due to decreased wavelength, sub-THz networks can increasingly operate in the near field, which yields non-planar wavefronts at receivers. In this paper, we present the first experimental study of receiver (RX) beamforming for sub-THz CoBF operating in the near field. Specifically, we introduce a suite of RX beamforming policies that span Channel State Information at the Receiver (CSIR) requirements as well as RX beamforming capabilities. At one extreme, we define a baseline RX beamforming policy that uses an electromagnetic wave model to compute CSIR, accounting for transmitter location, beam type, and near-field propagation characteristics; the RX then compensates for the computed phase profile over each RX array element to maximize coherent combining. At the other extreme, we consider strategies that, despite operating in the near field, employ far-field beam steering via a linear phase gradient at the receiver. Such policies are not only simple in CSIR requirements (not requiring phase information for each antenna element) but also simplify receiver configuration, requiring only a single parameter to characterize a linear phase gradient. We first experimentally study an unobstructed CoBF link and quantify the benefits of compensating for the nonlinear incident phase as compared to conventional far-field oriented methods. We then experimentally study obstructed links and measure the performance of the policies under partial blockage, as well as RX power improvement from real-time adaptation to blockage.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Windex: Index-Driven Contextual Scheduler for Scalable Service Guarantees in NextG Cellular Networks.
abstract: Next-generation cellular networks must support heterogeneous service objectives, ranging from throughput-oriented eMBB to latency- and regularity-constrained URLLC and XR traffic. Enforcing these objectives at the RAN scheduler is difficult because wireless channels, queues, and application arrivals evolve at the millisecond timescale while spectrum resources are shared across users. We formulate service-aware RAN scheduling as a constrained Markov decision process with per-user throughput and service-regularity constraints. A Lagrangian relaxation gives an exact decomposition of the relaxed problem into per-user control problems with a common resource price. We prove fixed-dual indexability for an illustrative time-since-last-service (TSLS) debt arm with a throughput objective and TSLS constraint, note the analogous scalar throughput-debt result, and assume fixed-dual indexability for the full vector state used in deployment. We design Windex, an index-driven scheduler that learns dual-dependent per-user break-even resource prices using compact neural approximators over queue, channel, TSLS, and violation-deficit state. We further design CWindex, a contextual extension that infers service class from queue-history time series when explicit labels are unavailable. We implement Windex as an application compatible with a realtime 5G radio intelligent controller. Inference takes 10-20 μs per user on a general-purpose CPU, well within a 1 ms control budget. Trace-driven emulation using over-the-air channel measurements and larger simulations show that Windex and CWindex substantially reduce per-user service violations while maintaining throughput efficiency.

title: Efficient Secure Federated Learning via Information-Theoretically Secure Key Distribution: A Medical Imaging Case Study.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of models across institutions without centralizing sensitive data, making it well-suited for privacy-concerned applications, such as medical imaging. To protect FL model updates during secure aggregation, additive masking is commonly employed. However, its underlying classical key establishment is only computationally secure. On the other hand, physics-based Information-Theoretically Secure (ITS) key exchange introduces practical constraints: finite key generation rates and time-limited storage severely limit throughput and sustained training of uncompressed models. In this work, we address this bottleneck by developing an FL framework that integrates frozen backbones, knowledge distillation, and quantization. These techniques reduce communication payload and, consequently, key material consumption. Moving beyond simulation, we benchmark this framework on a real physics-based key distribution testbed involving a chest X-ray classification application. Our results show that key usage can be reduced by ~35× while maintaining predictive accuracy. This prevents buffer depletion and key expiration, enabling sustainable FL training under physical key generation constraints.

title: Asymptotically Optimal Joint Generation-Planning and Transmission-Scheduling for Periodic Deadline-Constrained Wireless Communication.
abstract: We study the joint design of packet generation-planning and transmission-scheduling for periodic, deadline-constrained wireless communication. While transmission scheduling has been extensively studied in the literature, the generation planning problem has been largely neglected. However, a poor packet generation plan (e.g., when all sources generate new packets at the same time) causes high latency that cannot be overcome by transmission scheduling alone. We propose a new joint offline-online optimization framework for this problem, in which generation timing is optimized offline to spread arrivals evenly across time, while online transmission decisions are made via a Whittle index scheduling policy. Interestingly, we find that the Whittle index policy by itself (obtained through a standard relaxed problem) may not be asymptotically optimal given an arbitrary generation plan. Instead, it becomes asymptotically optimal only after we jointly design the generation plan (based on the solution to the same relaxed problem). We prove that our joint solution is asymptotically optimal under assumptions/conditions of uniform global attractivity, uniform local stability, and peak-smoothing. Our proof requires new techniques that capture the periodic and time-inhomogeneous nature of the system and that overcome the difficulty due to the generation plans changing with the system scale. We verify our stated assumptions and optimality results through simulations, and show that our joint solution achieves substantially lower latency plus deadline-violation costs than other baselines.

title: PRISM: Reinforced Semantic Communication for Decentralized Federated Anomaly Detection in Vehicular Networks.
abstract: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) enables collaborative learning that preserves privacy, but faces critical communication challenges in bandwidth-constrained environments such as vehicular networks. We propose Policy-driven Representation and Information Selection Method (PRISM), a Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based method that optimizes semantic communication in DFL through adaptive representation selection and intelligent topology management. Our dual-model architecture separates task learning (autoencoder-based anomaly detection) from communication control (Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based decision making), enabling agents to dynamically select between transmitting full model weights or compressed trajectory embeddings. We formulate this as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) and train using a Centralized Training Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm. We demonstrate our method through a digital twin monitoring scenario where vehicles collaboratively detect trajectory anomalies in neighbors' behavior in real time, and the logged detections support forensic analysis, insurance claims, and fleet auditing. Experiments on Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) generated Barcelona traffic data show an F1-score of 0.90, scaling from 2 to 128 agents with graceful degradation past N = 32, Byzantine-robust aggregation, and validation on Next Generation Simulation (NGSIM) US-101 real traces (F1 0.82). The learned policy exhibits emergent temporal behavior: transmitting weights early during training when model divergence is high, then shifting to embeddings as models converge, with the weight-to-embedding mix derived as the equilibrium of the communication budget constraint. The method generalizes to other bandwidth-limited collaborative learning domains.

title: Optimal Parallel Scheduling under Concave Speedup Functions.
abstract: Efficiently scheduling parallel computing resources across multiple concurrent jobs is a core challenge in modern cloud and edge computing systems that support AI-driven applications. Allocating more resources to a job accelerates its completion, but with diminishing returns. Prior work (heSRPT) has solved this problem for certain speedup functions with an exponential form, providing a closed-form solution. However, the general case with arbitrary concave speedup functions—which more accurately capture real-world workloads—has remained open. In this paper, we solve this open problem by developing optimal scheduling algorithms for parallel jobs under general concave speedup functions. We first discover a fundamental and broadly-applicable rule for optimal parallel scheduling, namely the Consistent Derivative Ratio (CDR) Rule , which states that the ratio of the derivatives of the speedup functions across active jobs remains constant over time. To efficiently compute the optimal allocations that satisfy the CDR Rule, we propose the General Water-Filling (GWF) method, a more general version of classical water-filling in wireless communications. Combining these insights, we design the SmartFill Algorithm to solve the general scheduling problem. Unlike heSRPT, which always allocates resources to all active jobs, SmartFill selectively determines which jobs should receive resources and how much they should be allocated. For a broad class of so-called regular speedup functions, SmartFill yields closed-form optimal solutions, while for non-regular functions it efficiently computes the optimum numerically. Simulation results show that SmartFill can outperform heSRPT across a wide range of concave speedup functions.

title: Receiver-Aware Token Routing for Semantic Communication.
abstract: Mission-critical mobile networks increasingly support AI-enabled services under heterogeneous and degraded wireless conditions. Semantic communication offers a promising approach by transmitting compact task-relevant representations, but most existing methods remain receiver-agnostic. We propose a receiver-aware semantic routing framework that combines hard receiver-conditioned token gating with learned mixture-of-experts transformation. A shared Vision Transformer extracts patch-level tokens, while a receiver-conditioned router jointly produces token-selection scores and expert-routing logits. Hard Top-K gating determines which routed token representations contribute to semantic aggregation, and soft expert routing adapts token representations to the receiver profile. Experiments on the MS COCO multi-label recognition task under high-SNR, low-SNR, and constrained token-retention conditions show consistent gains over static conditioning, random token selection, and pruning baselines. The results demonstrate that jointly controlling token retention and receiver-aware semantic transformation improves semantic inference under the evaluated AWGN and token-retention conditions.

title: Pushing Bistatic Wireless Sensing toward High Accuracy at the Sub-Wavelength Scale.
abstract: Contactless sensing using wireless communication signals has garnered significant attention due to its non-intrusive nature and ubiquitous infrastructure. Despite the promise, the inherent bistatic deployment of wireless communication introduces clock asynchronism, which leads to unknown phase offsets in channel response and hinders fine-grained sensing. State-of-the-art systems widely adopt the cross-antenna channel response ratio to cancel these detrimental phase offsets. However, the channel response ratio preserves sensing feature accuracy only at integer-wavelength target displacements, losing sub-wavelength fidelity. To overcome this limitation, we derive the first quantitative mapping between the distorted ratio feature and the ideal-channel sensing feature. Building on this foundation, we develop a robust framework that leverages raw channel response amplitude to recover the ideal sensing feature from the distorted ratio. Real-world experiments across Wi-Fi and LoRa signals demonstrate that our method can effectively reconstruct sub-wavelength displacement details, achieving nearly an order-of-magnitude improvement in accuracy.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: MIRA: An Edge-Cloud Multimodal LLM Framework for DESH Assessment in IoT-Enabled MRI Workflows.
abstract: Connected MRI scanners operate as networked medical devices within DICOM-based healthcare Internet of Things (IoT) workflows, but conventional connectivity primarily moves images to a Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) rather than adding task-specific reasoning near acquisition. Building on DESH-App 2.0, a preceding machine-learning contribution accepted for oral presentation at SIN Firenze 2026, this paper specifies MIRA (Multimodal Imaging Reasoning and Assessment), a vendor-neutral edge-cloud module for assessing disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid spaces (DESH). A hospital-edge gateway validates and de-identifies 3D T1-weighted DICOM studies, derives ventricular, high-convexity, and Sylvian-fissure masks with SegFormer3D, and converts each volume into a compact evidence package comprising 12 representative slices with overlays, 17 global, zonal, and ratio features, and quality-control tokens. LLaVA-Med-7B and Lingshu-7B are adapted through 4-bit QLoRA to return constrained JSON containing class, confidence, named anatomical evidence, and an abstention or quality warning. The edge-cloud partition keeps raw volumes inside the institutional network; only the compact evidence package may reach an authenticated inference service, while structured outputs return to the PACS workstation. The evaluation protocol jointly covers diagnostic discrimination, calibration, evidence agreement, unsupported claims, abstention, latency, transmitted bytes, memory demand, link-loss recovery, and multi-device interoperability. MIRA is designed to add auditable multimodal reasoning to connected MRI workflows without modifying safety-critical scanner controls.

title: BrewSense: A Mobile Water Quality Monitoring Platform using Laser Reflection near Brewster Angle.
abstract: BrewSense is a mobile water-quality monitoring platform for realtime, large-scale detection of inland water pollution beyond the reach of grab sampling and remote sensing, whose alternatives are invasive, expensive, or limited to narrow classes of solutes and controlled environments. BrewSense leverages laser reflection near Brewster's angle to remotely infer the refractive index of surface water, which varies approximately linearly with the concentration of both ionic and organic solutes. It combines a beam-splitter and orthogonal-polarizer front-end that strongly suppresses ambient light, synchronized electrodynamic indexers with magnetic angle sensing, and hierarchical angular sampling, Gaussian spot filtering, and derivative-based Brewster-angle fitting that stabilize measurements under platform motion, waves, turbidity, and temperature variations. Implemented on a UAV, BrewSense operates at meter-scale standoff distances and achieves sub-10-4 refractive-index resolution under controlled conditions. Controlled and real-lake-water tank experiments evaluate inorganic salts (NaCl, NH4Cl) and organic solutes (glucose, urea), and a UAV deployment validates end-to-end operation in a NaCl-dominated field setting. BrewSense achieves up to 3.2× lower error than prior UWB and vibration-based systems and an approximately 8% mean relative concentration-estimation error across 20 UAV field sites.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Semantic-Aware Scheduling for Task-Oriented Communication by Mitigating Congestion in Emergency Networks.
abstract: Modern communication systems have fundamentally relied on bit-level perfect transmission, which becomes critically inefficient in resource-constrained disaster scenarios where bandwidth is scarce and timely information is paramount. The convergence of sensing, artificial intelligence, and communication is emerging as a key paradigm for next-generation networks, where semantic communication, transmitting the contextual meaning of data rather than raw bits, offers a promising solution. However, existing semantic approaches lack the integration of emergency-critical semantic extraction from visual sensors with semantic-aware network resource allocation. This paper bridges this gap by proposing a novel end-to-end semantic communication framework for congested emergency networks. We develop a task-oriented image captioning pipeline that fine-tunes a BLIP model on a custom-built dataset annotated with emergency-critical captions to convert sensed images into concise, actionable textual descriptions. Furthermore, we design a suite of semantic-aware MAC schedulers (specifically, DRR-Sorted, DRR-Boosted, DRR-Hybrid, and PF-Priority) that utilize content-derived priority tags to intelligently allocate network resources and mitigate congestion. Integrated into an OMNeT++/Simu5G simulation of a 5G mmWave network with a constrained backhaul, our framework delivers emergency information over 98% faster than traditional image transmission. This represents a paradigm shift from multi-second delays to near-instantaneous delivery of life-saving intelligence for first responders, demonstrating the practical benefits of tightly integrated sensing, AI, and communication pipelines.

title: Physics-Informed Kernelized Thompson Sampling for Beam Management in Millimeter-Wave Systems.
abstract: Maintaining connectivity in directional millimeter-wave communications requires frequent beam probing and realignment, incurring substantial overhead. We address this challenge by formulating beam tracking as a kernelized multi-armed bandit over the two-dimensional beam-angle domain. We propose GP-TSAF, a Gaussian process Thompson sampling algorithm with a physics-informed array-factor (AF) kernel. Derived directly from the known array geometry and beam codebook, the AF kernel captures beam-pattern overlap, including sidelobe interactions and null-induced decorrelation, without learning the beam-correlation structure from data. This allows each received signal strength (RSS) observation to update the posterior over the full codebook, enabling data-efficient tracking under limited measurements. To improve robustness under mobility, we further introduce adaptive correlation scaling, which weakens cross-beam smoothing as the prediction error increases without requiring an explicit mobility model. For a stationary fixed-kernel variant, we establish a cumulative-regret bound whose kernel-dependent complexity is characterized by the AF-kernel spectrum. Evaluation on 30 GHz simulation datasets with 32- and 64-beam codebooks and a 28 GHz over-the-air dataset with a 28-beam codebook shows that GP-TSAF achieves lower mean oracle gap and cumulative regret than several baselines.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Shear: Goal-Oriented Anomaly Detection on Compressed Time Series via Semantic Transition Graph.
abstract: Sensor data in IoT systems are commonly compressed to meet resource constraints, yet anomaly detection directly on compressed data remains largely unexplored. This challenge is particularly evident for recurrent anomalies, which commonly appear as repeated abnormal patterns in long-running IoT streams. Existing approaches often become cumbersome or expensive since they decouple compression from analytics, requiring detection to reprocess full raw data, while supervised deep learning alternatives further demand labels or incur computational overhead unsuitable for edge deployment. In this paper, we propose Shear, a goal-oriented unsupervised method via Semantic Transition Graph (STG) induced directly from compressed time series. The STG organizes compressed representation as semantic states and encodes their temporal transitions, so that recurrent anomaly patterns are identified through unlikely state transition chains without decompression or neural network inference. Experiments on public datasets show that Shear achieves better detection performance than state-of-the-art approaches, while running 3.9× to 11.2× faster than subsequence-oriented methods and up to 2219× faster than deep learning baselines, with substantially reduced storage and memory footprint.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Resource-Constrained Semantic-Aware Remote Estimation with Overlapping Sensor Coverage.
abstract: We study semantic-aware remote estimation of multiple finite-state Markov sources observed by K sensors with overlapping coverage. The sensors share a time-division multiple-access uplink and differ in transmission reliability, delivery delay, and transmission budget. In each slot, the scheduler jointly selects a source and one of its monitoring sensors, or remains idle, to minimize the long-run average cost of actuation error subject to global and per-sensor transmission-frequency constraints. We formulate this problem as a finite average-cost constrained Markov decision process. We show that the transmission resource functions have rank at most K. Consequently, the Lagrangian depends only on K effective transmission costs, and an optimal constrained solution can be represented using at most K +1 deterministic policy-recurrent-class components. We further characterize the piecewise-affine concave Lagrangian value function and derive projected dual subgradient ascent over an explicitly bounded multiplier set. Numerical results illustrate the value-function structure, the need for policy randomization in a representative instance, and the interaction between global and per-sensor transmission budgets.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: TSDM: A Scheduling Policy for Joint Throughput-AoI Optimization in Multichannel Wireless Networks.
abstract: Optimizing for both low Age of Information (AoI) and high throughput is critical for remote sensing applications that rely on multichannel wireless networks. However, jointly optimizing these two metrics is an analytically challenging problem, particularly in systems with heterogeneous and unreliable channels. To address this challenge, we propose TSDM, a Two-Stage Deficit Matching scheduling framework. TSDM is based on a second-order approach that characterizes the performance of each data flow by its mean and temporal variance. In the first stage, TSDM translates the highlevel utility maximization objective into a concrete set of target mean and temporal variance statistics for transmissions over each node-channel pair. In the second stage, a low-complexity Weighted Matching Deficit (WMD) rule performs real-time channel assignment. We theoretically prove that TSDM achieves the desired mean and temporal variance for each flow. Furthermore, we conduct extensive simulations on two open problems in joint throughput-AoI optimization. In both cases, TSDM significantly outperforms existing scheduling policies.

title: ECO-COMM: An Ultra Low-Latency Event Camera based Optical Communication System.
abstract: Ultra-low-latency communication is critical for emerging applications such as XR, real-time control, and distributed sensing. We present ECO-COMM, an event-camera-based optical communication system for ultra-low-latency device association and lightweight information exchange. By exploiting the asynchronous sensing and microsecond-level temporal resolution of event cameras, ECO-COMM captures high-frequency optical signals without frame-based acquisition delays. We identify and analyze key hardware-induced challenges in event-camera communication, including timestamp inconsistency, readout contention, trailing effects, and the inevitable refractory period, and develop hardware-aware mitigation techniques to address them. Focusing on a single transmitter-receiver optical link, ECO-COMM establishes the feasibility of practical ultra-low-latency event-camera communication using commercially available hardware. A prototype implementation using an eight-LED transmitter and an off-the-shelf event camera achieves device association within 15 μs, symbol latency as low as 100 μs, and end-to-end latency below 8 ms for 32-byte payloads at a 0.1% bit error rate. Overall, ECO-COMM establishes a practical and complementary communication paradigm for ultra-low-latency systems.

title: Skynet: Workflow-Level Anomaly Detection for Agentic AI via Semantic and Structural Modeling.
abstract: Agentic AI systems execute complex tasks through long-horizon workflows of planning, tool use, and multi-agent coordination. Task failures in these systems often originate from a single step, such as an injected prompt or a flawed plan, and are then amplified through downstream dependencies as the corrupted step propagates across many subsequent agents and tool calls. Existing defenses either target a specific class of attacks or failures, or inspect individual prompts and steps in isolation. Both leave the global dependency structure of a workflow unexamined, and miss the inconsistencies that only emerge when the execution is viewed as a whole. We argue that anomaly detection for agentic AI must reason at the workflow level, where global execution structure exposes signals that local checks cannot see. We present Skynet, a principled workflow-level anomaly detection framework that turns observed multi-agent execution into directed workflow graphs and scores them against learned benign behavior. Skynet jointly models the semantic execution context and the structural organization of inter-agent delegation, tool invocation, and data-flow dependencies, and trains only on benign workflows. Because training never sees attacks or failures, this design naturally extends to zero-day detection: any execution that violates benign workflow regularities surfaces as off-manifold geometry under a single decision rule. We evaluate Skynet on three public agentic safety and failure benchmarks. It sustains high recall together with a sub-1% false positive rate, with per-workflow and per-step latencies low enough for online monitoring of agentic AI runtimes.

title: MOSAIC: Efficient Collaborative Inference for Multi-Modal Large Language Models with Distributed Edge Computing.
abstract: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) enable natural language reasoning over heterogeneous sensory data, appealing to many edge AI scenarios, yet their deployment faces competing demands on latency, energy, and quality. We present MOSAIC, which adopts a component-level decomposition and distributed deployment paradigm for efficient MLLM inference at the edge, realizing three core ideas: parallel encoding, token pruning, and device-server collaboration. Specifically, for the offline stage, modality-specific encoders distilled from a unified foundation model are co-deployed with Q-Former projection on edge devices for parallel encoding, while LoRA instruction fine-tuning adapts the frozen LLM backbone to downstream tasks. For the online stage, we formulate a multi-objective optimization over latency and energy that jointly tunes token budgets, device frequencies, and quantization precision under long-term semantic accuracy constraints, achieving dynamic token pruning and device-server collaboration. We leverage Lagrangian relaxation to decompose the original problem into tractable per-slot subproblems and design an online algorithm with provable near-optimal performance and guaranteed constraint satisfaction. We implement a realistic testbed for extensive performance evaluation, which demonstrates that MOSAIC reduces latency by up to 49.8% and energy by up to 65.1% over advanced baselines while maintaining high semantic accuracy.
